title: Getting Around
tagline: Directions, taking a rickshaw, haggling and ordering food.
canDo: You can get around a Pakistani city: directions, fares, ordering

grammar.title: Commands: -o vs -iye
grammar.body: Tum form: stem + o (ruko, baitho, chalo). Aap form: stem + iye (rukiye, baithiye, chaliye). A softer aap form ends in -ein (rukein, chalein). Irregular: karo/kijiye (do), lo/lijiye (take), do/dijiye (give).

grammar.title: Postpositions
grammar.body: Urdu has 'post'-positions: they come after the noun. mein (in), par (on/at), se (from), tak (until), ko (to). Place words take ke: ghar ke paas (near the house), dukaan ke saamne (in front of the shop), masjid ke peeche (behind the mosque).

phrases.note: Everyone in Pakistan says 'washroom'. Asking for the 'toilet' gets a wince.

teach.title: Two ways to tell someone to do something
teach.info: To a friend or kid: stem + o (ruko, baitho, chalo). To an elder or stranger: stem + iye (rukiye, baithiye, chaliye). Same verb, different respect level.

teach.title: Postpositions
teach.info: English puts 'near' before the noun. Urdu puts it after, with ke: ghar ke paas (house near), dukaan ke saamne (shop in-front-of), masjid ke peeche (mosque behind). 'In' is just mein: bazaar mein.

lessons.title: Kitna kiraya?
lessons.blurb: Haggling: the sacred dance between you and every rickshaw-wala.
lessons.canDo: You can negotiate a fare without being fleeced (much)

teach.title: The haggling script
teach.info: 1. Ask if they'll go. 2. Ask the fare. 3. Gasp. 4. Counter at about half. 5. Walk away if needed. 6. They call you back. Never skip the gasp.

boss.title: Pervez and the Fare
boss.blurb: You need to get to the bazaar. Pervez has a rickshaw, a price, and no change.
boss.scene: Lahore, 4pm, 38°C. A rickshaw sputters to a stop in front of you. The driver, Pervez, leans out with the confidence of a man who has never lost a negotiation.
boss.canDo: You can haggle a rickshaw fare and give directions on the way

b.prompt: Ask if he'll go to the bazaar (and how much).

options.reaction: The gasp was perfect. He nods with grudging respect.
You accepted the first price. Somewhere, every Pakistani aunty felt a disturbance.

f.prompt: He says 300 is final. Is it?

options.reaction: You turn and walk. One step. Two steps…

h.prompt: He's driving like it's a Fast & Furious audition.

end.title: Fare negotiated
end.text: You haggled, survived the drive and got out in one piece. Pervez didn't have change, obviously. You'll call it a tip.
